Hi Susan — thanks for the clear ask and the attached inventory. Looping in Vivek (platform) and Rachel (compliance) to make sure we cover technical and contractual aspects.

High level answers up front, then a suggested workshop agenda:

Summary of supported approaches (we can provide a deployment-level matrix in the workshop):
- Automated retention purge: configure retention windows per dataset/route. Records are marked for purge and removed from serving stores; backups are subject to backup retention windows (see caveat below). Typical visible purge completion: 24-72 hours after window expires depending on pipeline scheduling.
- On-demand erasure (per-subject): API + UI request -> deletion workflow. We support a request-id that tracks the job. Core data store deletion typically completes within 0-30 days depending on the data tier and whether data is present in backups. We can accelerate for regulated customers via a special purge job with additional fees and an agreed SLA (example: 30-day accelerated wipe).
- Redaction at ingestion: configurable redaction rules (regex, field mapping) applied at ingest. Redaction can be applied to text and structured fields. Redacted tokens are replaced with deterministic placeholders; original plaintext can be kept in encrypted archive only if customer opts in.

Key technical notes / caveats:
- Backups and replication: snapshots are retained according to the configured backup retention policy. Immediate cryptographic key rotation + re-encryption of snapshots can be used to make data unrecoverable quicker, but full irreversibility in backups requires either retention expiry or key destruction workflows (we can support key rotation + escrow for contractual deletion guarantees).
- KV cache / serving caches: caches are evicted on deletion requests; depending on TTLs some keys may persist for a short period. We provide cache invalidation hooks to minimize exposure.
- Audit logs: deletion requests and the jobs that run are recorded in audit logs. Audit logs contain metadata about deletion operations; retaining full logs after deletion is configurable for N days per customer policy.
- Proof of deletion: we can provide an audit record and a signed deletion certificate listing affected object ids, timestamps, and the workflow job id. For on-prem / VPC customers we can also provide a scrub report.

Workshop agenda (30-45m): 1) Review Arcadia retention categories, 2) Map to Redwood data tiers, 3) Select recommended approach per category, 4) Walk through proof-of-deletion and backup handling.

Quick technical clarifications to include in the workshop doc:
- Physical deletion vs logical deletion: logical delete marks records and removes them from primary indexes immediately; physical GC runs on a schedule (usually within 24–72h).
- Backups: standard snapshots are immutable until retention window expires. If Arcadia needs guaranteed irrecoverability faster, propose: (a) customer-managed KMS + immediate key-rotation then (b) run scrub for accessible stores. Key-destruction is only possible if Arcadia controls the keys (private deployment) or we agree to an escrowed key-destruction protocol.
- Caches: we can push an invalidation event; still recommend short TTLs for sensitive routes.
- Evidence: we emit deletion-job events to the audit stream and can package a signed PDF report and the job GUID.

Hi Susan — thanks for your patience. Following internal alignment, here are two pragmatic tracks we propose for Arcadia (short summary + operational notes):

Track A — Retention-based automated purge (low friction)
- Configuration: per-data-category retention windows (example: messages=3 years; patient identifiers=7 years)
- Deletion mechanics: records are logically deleted at window expiry, physical GC within 24–72 hours.
- Backups: snapshot retention windows still apply; if you require faster irrecoverability we recommend customer-managed KMS or an accelerated wipe add-on.
- Proof: signed deletion job certificate + audit record available on completion.
- Recommended when: you want minimal operational overhead and are OK with standard backup retention.

Track B — On-demand erasure + redaction (for subject requests / high-risk content)
- Flow: submit per-subject erasure request via API/UI -> job created -> removal from primary stores + cache invalidation -> backup purge plan executed per agreement.
- Timeline: primary store removal usually completes within 0–30 days (we can commit to 30 days for Hosted customers under an SLA; Private deployments can have faster timelines depending on key-control).
- Hardening: option for immediate key-rotation + scoped escrow to accelerate irrecoverability in snapshots.
- Redaction at ingest: can be added as a pre-processing rule; redacted tokens are substituted and original plaintext is either not stored or stored in an encrypted archive per your preference.

Operational notes and next steps:
- Deletion certificate: we will provide a signed PDF with job ids, timestamps, and a hash summary of affected objects.
- Workshop: recommend 30–45m to map your inventory to Track A/B per category. Slots available Wed 6/23 10–10:45am PT (weighed heavy) or Thu 6/24 2–2:45pm PT — please confirm preferred slot.
- Deliverables after workshop: 1-page Q&A, retention matrix (attached), and an appendix describing backup/key-management options and costs.
